steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Note-taking: write DURING the performance — focus on specific moments, not general impressions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Four areas to analyse: performance (acting), design (set, costume, lighting, sound), direction (staging, pacing), and overall intention.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always identify WHAT you saw, HOW it was done, and WHAT EFFECT it had on the audience.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Use precise terminology: 'proscenium arch' not 'normal stage'; 'gobo' not 'light pattern'; 'blocking' not 'where they stood'.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What should you focus on when taking notes during a live theatre performance? | Explain the difference between DESCRIBING a moment and ANALYSING it. Why does analysis score higher marks? | How would you structure your analysis of a key moment from a production you have seen?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Specific moments, not general impressions. Record: what happened, which techniques were used, how the audience responded. Focus on performance (vocal/physical choices), design (set, lighting, costume, | Description: 'The actor shouted loudly.' Analysis: 'The actor increased volume to a shout and broke previously measured pacing, conveying the character's loss of control and shocking the audience into | Identify the moment precisely; describe the theatrical techniques used; explain the intended effect on the audience; evaluate how successful the choices were; link to the production's overall intentio

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Write notes DURING the performance, not after — details fade quickly Focus on SPECIFIC moments, not general impressions of the whole show Always use precise theatrical terminology — examiners reward vocabulary Link every observation to EFFECT on the audience
